messages:
maya: Heads up — since ~02:20 UTC we're seeing a spike in Pending pods for GPU workloads. ~120 pods in Pending across two clusters, reason=0/1 nvidia.com/gpu: insufficient resources and scattered small free GPUs across nodes.
eli: Saw it too. Packable-looking fragmentation: lots of nodes with 1–2 free GPU slices but pods request 4/8 GPUs. Cluster-autoscaler didn't add nodes because there's headroom in nodes just not contiguous.
jorge: Do we have the auto-provisioner set to consider 'consolidatable' nodes? CA ignores fragmentation.
lin: No, CA doesn't do binpacking consolidation. We rely on rebalancer job but it's disabled during business hours.
sam: Can we run an immediate repack? I have a script to migrate smaller GPU jobs to a temporary nodepool.
maya: Yes, we need a short-term mitigation + config change. Short-term: create a small-gpu nodepool (p4d-8ish) and drain low-priority pods onto it to free up A100 nodes.
eli: I can cordon/drain a few nodes. Command I'll run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
sam: Reminder: use --pod-selector to only evict pods in gpu-namespace that are safe to restart.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-198 — GPU scheduling fragmentation impacting ml-prod-cluster. Pager duty notified.
maya: Cost callout — if we spin up a smaller nodepool it'll increase hourly cost but should avoid failing training jobs. We need to weigh against SLA hit for product experiments.
jorge: Medium-term: update cluster-autoscaler config to support scale-up when fragmentation prevents placement. There's a CA flag we can tune (expander/policy?) but not trivial.
lin: Also propose a packing controller: periodic assessor that labels nodes as 'low-frag' and triggers a consolidation cron.
eli: For today I'm going to migrate ~30 low-priority pods to a new p4d-small nodepool and then uncordon nodes. ETA 25m. I'll post progress.
sam: I'll prepare RBAC + nodepool terraform change so we can create the pool quickly.
maya: Post-mortem action items: 1) enable rebalancer during off-hours with faster cooldown, 2) add CA fragmentation heuristic, 3) add admission hook to prefer exact-GPU requests when possible, 4) run a one-off compact job weekly.
jorge: For admission hook — we should reject pods that request > available contiguous GPUs per node type and suggest right-sizing. Could be a webhook that returns a helpful message.
lin: Also plan to add a metric: 'gpu_fragmentation_ratio' per nodepool so autoscaler can trigger on it.
eli: Update: started drain of gpu-node-42, eviction is ongoing (12/18 pods evicted). Patching cloudscheduler to prefer placement on p4d-small.
maya: Thanks. Also, add a temporary label to the A100 pool so scaling policies don't over-provision while we rebalance: `kubectl label nodepool a100-pool temp-rebalance=true` (ops only).
sam: Terraform snippet for new pool (in #infra-terraform repo):
```
resource "cloud_nodepool" "p4d_small" {
  name = "p4d-small-repack"
  machine_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  replicas = 2
  labels = { purpose = "repack" }
}
```
maya: Who owns follow-up to change CA behaviour? jorge?
jorge: I'll take it, will draft a design doc and link to this thread. Plan: add fragmentation-aware scale-up + consolidation signal. Target PR in two weeks.
eli: Drain complete for two nodes, freed 8 GPUs — starting rollout of queued jobs now. Observability: unsched pods dropped from 120 -> 40.
maya: Great. Keep an eye on cost dashboard. If burst adds >20% burn for >3 hours we switch to throttling non-critical jobs.
sam: Noted. I'll monitor billing and add alerts.
maya: Closing loop: ops-bot, please add INC-2026-198 to postmortems and assign to eng-infra.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-198 updated: assigned_to=eng-infra, severity=minor, link=https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-198
eli: tl;dr: temporary nodepool + drains fixed immediate surge, jorge owns longer-term autoscaler changes, sam owns infra change + cost alerting.
maya: Thanks all — will follow up with the design doc and schedule a sync to review the autoscaler changes.
